title: Reflection Questions for a Simpler, Clearer Calendar
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Dave Stuart Jr. shares three reflection questions that he and his wife use to audit their calendar before re-committing to activities as pandemic-era restrictions loosen. Rooted in his broader philosophy of simplicity and human finitude, the piece argues that most people over-commit not from bad intentions but from failing to periodically ask whether a recurring commitment is actually producing what they hoped it would. The three questions move from noticing a commitment that feels good in theory but bad in practice, to imagining what withdrawal from it might cost and gain, to surfacing invisible time-consuming habits (news, social media, television) that never made it onto the calendar in the first place but arguably should. Stuart frames the exercise as a corrective to a culture that pushes constant addition rather than periodic subtraction. The post is a condensed excerpt of a longer paid webinar he was promoting at the time.
points: A recurring commitment deserves periodic re-evaluation against a simple emotional test: does seeing it on the calendar produce refreshment and excitement, or anxiety and resentment?
Before withdrawing from a commitment, it helps to concretely imagine both the worst-case cost and the best-case benefit of stepping away, even if only for a season.

Invisible time-consumers like news, social media, and television often escape scrutiny simply because they were never formally scheduled; naming them as if they were calendar commitments makes their true cost visible.
The practice of simplicity is less about willpower and more about periodically auditing commitments against what they were actually meant to produce.
quotes: Since the COVID closures of spring 2020, I've longed to deepen the degree to which the practice of simplicity is an integrated part of my life.
Because I'm finite — and you are, too. There's only so much we can do, so much we can think about, so many tasks we can accomplish, so many efficiencies we can uncover.

Ask: Am I seeing that these commitments are actually producing what I hoped would be produced? Is the impact I hoped this would have really happening? When I see this on my calendar, do I feel refreshed and excited… or anxious or resentful?

What would be the worst thing to happen if I withdrew from this commitment — if only for a season? What would be the best thing that could happen from withdrawing from this? What unexpected benefits might there be?

Here we're trying to make visible the invisible habits that can consume an hour per day of our lives. I'm talking news, social media, recurring, superficial conversations, television, Netflix, games on your phone, etc.
If I had to calendarize this — to see it on my calendar each day as a place where my time is going, a commitment I'm making — would I like that or not?
